title: Concurrent experiment allocations can share one output directory
reasoning: Directory discovery and creation are separate operations. Concurrent callers can observe the same maximum suffix and both choose the same next path. Because mkdir uses exist_ok=True, both report success and receive the same output directory, allowing independent experiments to mix or overwrite artifacts.
reproduction: Synchronize two callers after they enumerate an empty experiment directory. Both select exp_001 and both return successfully with that same path.
recommendation: Reserve candidate directories with exclusive mkdir and retry allocation on FileExistsError, or serialize allocation with an interprocess lock.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included test invokes get_next_experiment_dir, and there is no concurrent allocation coverage.
suggestedRegressionTest: Run multiple synchronized allocators against one parent and assert all successful calls return distinct, newly created directories.
minimumFixScope: get_next_experiment_dir reservation logic and concurrent allocation tests.

Concurrent callers selecting the same candidate therefore cannot both return it. tests/utils_test.py:12 adds eight concurrent allocators and asserts distinct, newly created directories.
